start.editing: Use the editor’s // button to comment or uncomment selected lines and ≡ to format the file. Open files can be arranged in tabs or separate windows.
start.introduction: BlueK runs Kotlin in your browser. You can run a program through main or create objects and call their methods directly.
start.createProject: Choose New Project for an empty project, a template or a demo. Use Open / Import for an existing project.
start.createFile: Choose New File, enter a name and select its type. Double-click a card to edit its code.
start.compile: Click Compile. Errors link to their file and line.
start.run: Right-click a class to create an object, or click Start main to run an entry point.
start.export: Use Save / Export → Export Project JSON to keep a portable copy.
start.firstObject: Create a Counter, call increment() from its context menu and double-click the object to inspect value.
start.diagram: Diagram: files and classes. Drag cards to arrange them; use the inheritance tool to select a subclass, then its superclass.
start.codepad: Codepad: Kotlin expressions and statements. The arrow beside the bench shows or hides it.
start.terminal: Terminal: program output and input. Its top-right icon cycles between closed, window and split views.
start.viewIcons: View icons: terminal, inheritance arrows and test-class visibility.
start.utilities: Bottom-left icons: offline download, Help and Settings. Settings controls dark mode, editor font size and Vim mode.
start.main: Choose Kotlin Functions in New File and write fun main() { /* your code */ }. Start main is disabled without an entry point. With several entry points, choose the file each time. main(args: Array<String>) receives an empty array.
start.freshSession: Compile creates a fresh session and clears live objects and codepad variables. Source changes require recompilation. Stop ends a running operation, including an endless loop or input wait.

objects.returnedValues: A returned value appears in a result dialog. Get gives it a name on the bench. Get preserves object identity.
objects.inputOutput: print and println write to the terminal. readln(), readLine() and readlnOrNull() wait for input there. Submit a line or use the terminal's EOF control. Stop cancels the wait.
objects.constructorsAndMethods: Right-click a class to choose a constructor. Enter a name and Kotlin expressions for its arguments. Right-click a bench object to call a method. Clicking another bench object can insert its name into an argument field.
objects.inspection: Double-click an object to see its properties. Follow references to inspect connected objects. Field edits accept Kotlin expressions.
objects.inspectionEffects: Opening or refreshing the inspector evaluates getters. A getter may have effects or throw an exception. Automatic inspection is excluded from saved state and test recording. Removing an object from the bench hides or releases its name; references held by other objects may still keep it alive.
objects.codepadExecution: Press Enter to run a statement or expression. Declarations remain available until Compile or Reset.

projects.recentWork: Open / Import → Recent work opens saved drafts. The trash icons and Delete all remove browser copies after confirmation. Open projects stay open; later edits can save them again.
projects.linkOptions: Both link types share Open README and Load state options. Load state requires a default test class. JSON imports do not load state automatically.
projects.offline: Open the download icon, download and extract the ZIP, then open BlueK.html in a recent browser. No installation is needed. Short links require the online service; full links open online BlueK. Moving the HTML file may make its browser drafts unavailable.
projects.autosave: BlueK automatically saves project source, resources, README, diagram positions and the default state class in this browser. Each tab updates one independent draft. Reload restores it. Live objects are not autosaved: use Saved state to recreate them.
projects.retention: Drafts have no BlueK expiry date, but browser cleanup, private browsing or storage limits can remove them. Export JSON for work you need to keep or transfer to another browser.
projects.import: Open a BlueK JSON file, or import a BlueJ project ZIP or folder. Kotlin, positions and resources are imported; Java source cannot run.
projects.jsonExport: Save an editable project with its resources and test/state classes.
projects.fullLink: Encode the project in a URL. Large projects may exceed the link size limit.
projects.shortLink: Store the project on the share service for 30 days. Anyone with the link can open it.
projects.htmlExport: Create a standalone program page that runs its main without BlueK.
projects.linkReload: Opening a project link replaces this tab's draft and removes the project payload from the address bar. Reload keeps your changes. To start from the original again, open the original link explicitly.
projects.resources: Click the document in the diagram to edit the project's README using Markdown. Name the project in the top bar. In BluePlay projects, add WAV or MP3 sounds with the Audio button in the toolbar; your own sounds can be renamed or removed there, the built-in ones cannot. Add PNG or JPEG images the same way with the Images button; transparent PNG pixels do not collide, a JPEG collides as a full rectangle.
projects.offlineCaution: The offline version has had limited practical testing. Check your projects and browser before relying on it, and keep JSON backups.

state.save: Use Save state below the bench. The first save suggests StateTest as the class name.
state.review: Review the code, then choose Save & Compile. Saving clears the live bench.
state.recordedActions: Constructors, method calls, explicit property reads, assignments and supported codepad steps become val properties and setup code. Automatic inspector reads are excluded. Shared references remain shared. Removed objects and intermediate results become local variables only when later preparation needs them.
state.replacement: Saving over existing preparation replaces all class properties, all @BeforeTest methods and init blocks. BlueK warns before replacing them. Other methods, including @Test methods, stay.
state.introduction: Save state stores the preparation needed to recreate your objects as ordinary Kotlin in a test class. You do not need a test method to use it.
state.prepare: Create objects and prepare them through method calls, assignments or the codepad.
state.buttonsTitle: The three buttons below the bench
state.saveButton: Write the current preparation to the default class.
state.loadButton: Compile, create the default class and run its setup.
state.classButton: Select another class for both actions. Empty test classes are eligible.
state.defaultClass: The default is saved with the project. A test card’s context menu saves or loads that class.
state.replayLimits: Loading repeats the saved actions; it is not a snapshot of every value in memory. Random values, time, input and external effects can differ. Main execution and BluePlay simulation steps are not recorded. Primitive bench values are excluded; String references are supported.
state.failedActions: After a failed action, partial changes may remain. Reset and prepare the state again. BlueK rejects actions it cannot reconstruct.

tests.assertions: assertEquals(expected, actual), assertNotEquals(illegal, actual), assertTrue(condition), assertFalse(condition), assertNull(value), assertNotNull(value) and fail(). Each accepts an optional message. Additional overloads and assertions such as assertFailsWith are unsupported.
tests.introduction: Testing in BlueK is in alpha. Tests use a reduced kotlin.test API and run in the browser interpreter.
tests.createClasses: Right-click a class and choose Create Test Class for an attached green card. Use New File → Test Class for a free card. Attached cards move with their class.
tests.run: Expand the arrow below Start main. Tests… opens the class and test list, including empty classes. Use Run All Tests or a test card’s Run Tests. Results show passed, failed or ignored tests, error details and source navigation. Stop aborts the remaining tests.
tests.recordStart: Choose Record Test… for a class. BlueK loads its saved state first.
tests.recordActions: Perform the actions to test. Use Add Assertion in a method-result dialog to check equality, null or non-null.
tests.recordFinish: Choose Finish Recording…, review the generated method and save it.
tests.recordCancel: Cancel Recording discards the recording, but leaves changes made to live objects. Editing source or compiling ends the recording.
tests.testAnnotation: A public, parameterless instance method returning Unit.
tests.beforeAnnotation: Prepare a fresh test-class instance before each test.
tests.afterAnnotation: Clean up after setup or a test, including failures after setup begins.
tests.ignoreAnnotation: Skip a method or the whole class.
tests.limits: At most one BeforeTest and AfterTest per class. Test classes need a parameterless constructor and cannot have inheritance or type parameters. There are no BeforeAll/AfterAll, parameterized or nested tests. Each run recompiles and clears interactive objects; top-level state is shared within a run.

kotlin.imports: No package declarations, Java source, java.*/javax.* imports or arbitrary external libraries. Imports must come from supported kotlin.* APIs.
kotlin.constructors: Secondary constructors can delegate to this(...), but not super(...).
kotlin.references: Details: Kotlin compatibility reference and standard-library reference.
kotlin.introduction: BlueK interprets a subset of Kotlin, with language and library differences from Kotlin/JVM.
kotlin.files: Each project file contains one class, interface or enum, or top-level functions and properties. Executable top-level statements belong in the codepad.
kotlin.unsupportedDeclarations: No object expressions, named companion objects, typealias or fun interface.
kotlin.typeInference: Some smart casts, generic inference and standard-library overloads are missing. An explicit type or cast can help.
kotlin.initialization: Top-level properties initialize in file order; reading one too early fails.

blueplay.introduction: BluePlay provides worlds, actors, images, keyboard/mouse input and sound. Choose a BluePlay template or demo in New Project. Its library cards are read-only; double-click one for signatures and API help.
blueplay.controls: Act performs one step. Run/Pause repeats steps; Speed controls their rate. Each step calls the world's act and then its actors' act methods. Pause before using the codepad or object operations.
blueplay.reset: Reset calls the selected main again in the current session. It does not reinitialize top-level properties. Showing a world pauses it.
blueplay.properties: Use Kotlin properties: actor.image = Image("duck.png"). World requires width, height and cellSize. Add an actor with world.addObject(actor, x, y). Accessing actor.world before adding it throws an exception.
blueplay.worldApi: Size and background; show, act, addObject, removeObject, getObjects, getObjectsAt and showText.
blueplay.actorApi: x, y, rotation, image and world; act, move, turn, turnTowards, collision queries and edge/click checks.
blueplay.imageApi: Create a blank image, load a resource or copy an image; draw shapes/text/images, scale and change transparency.
blueplay.resources: Standard images such as duck.png, cat.png and pizza.png are included. Imported project resources with the same path take precedence. BluePlay's standard sounds such as explosion.wav, jump.wav and pickup.wav are included as well. playSound("pickup.wav") plays a sound from sounds/ once; sounds may overlap. Reset and Compile stop playing sounds.
blueplay.limits: The browser API excludes JVM/AWT internals and file access. Fonts and text collision are approximate. Saving preparation can replay object creation and explicit calls, but cannot preserve a running simulation.

shortcuts.introduction: Use Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Formatting and commenting act on the current Kotlin editor.

troubleshooting.aProgramIsWaitingOrWillNotFinish: A program is waiting or will not finish
troubleshooting.aCallFailedAfterChangingAnObject: A call failed after changing an object
troubleshooting.theGeneratedStateCannotBeSaved: The generated state cannot be saved
troubleshooting.reporting: report a bug on GitHub. Include a small project, the steps to reproduce it, the error and your browser/version.
troubleshooting.main: Add a top-level main function in a functions file, then compile. Class methods are not entry points.
troubleshooting.sessionReset: Compile, test runs and state saving start fresh sessions. Load state to recreate saved preparation.
troubleshooting.stop: Check the terminal for an input request. Use Stop for an endless loop or to cancel execution.
troubleshooting.failedCalls: Changes made before the error remain. Compile or Reset and repeat the preparation if you need a clean state.
troubleshooting.getters: A property getter failed. Inspect its error details; check whether the object needs initialization or world membership.
troubleshooting.drafts: Check Recent work in the same browser and site. Use an exported JSON file if browser data was removed.
troubleshooting.stateSave: Reset and repeat the preparation using actions supported by saved state.
